Ultra-realistic 8K DSLR photo of a 23-year-old Brazilian female influencer, 160cm height, with a naturally curvy and harmonious body, standing in a vibrant urban bar setting with strong Brazilian cultural elements.

Her skin has a warm golden-brown tone with extremely realistic texture: visible pores, subtle acne marks and natural imperfections, soft oil sheen on forehead, nose, shoulders and collarbones, micro skin variations and slight sweat glow from warm ambient lighting. No smoothing, no artificial skin — fully human realism.

Her face is highly detailed and expressive, with almond-shaped dark brown eyes, visible iris detail, subtle light reflection in pupils, full lips with natural hydration and slight gloss, well-defined cheekbones, and natural eyebrows with individual hairs visible. Expression is confident and slightly introspective, looking sideways (not directly at camera), creating a strong editorial feel.

Hair & Styling:
Hair tied back in a sleek bun, slightly imperfect with loose strands and natural frizz. Baby hairs visible along hairline. Subtle shine from warm light reflections.

Outfit:

Tight yellow cropped tank top with green trim and “BRAZIL” text (slightly worn fabric texture, realistic cotton fibers visible)

Camouflage pants with natural folds, creases, and fabric weight

Slight compression and interaction between clothing and body (waist, hips, torso)

Accessories (HIGH DETAIL):

Gold hoop earrings with realistic reflections

Multiple gold necklaces with small pendants (metal texture, micro scratches visible)

Gold bracelet and arm cuff

Visible small tattoos on arm and torso (fine lines, slightly faded ink realism)

Eyeglasses with transparent lenses reflecting ambient light and environment

🔥 Pose & Expression (EDITORIAL PRESENÇA)
Body slightly angled

One hand touching hair/head

Shoulders relaxed but confident

Chin slightly raised

Gaze directed sideways (cinematic mood)

Environment:
Bar/backdrop composed of stacked beverage crates (Ambev, Skol, Heineken style), colorful signage (“Seja bem-vindo”), bottles and textures in background.

👉 IMPORTANT:
Everything must be 100% in focus — crates, labels, textures, scratches, dust, reflections — NO blur, NO bokeh.

Lighting:
Warm artificial lighting mixed with colored reflections from signage.

Soft shadows on face and body

Highlights on skin and accessories

Slight contrast between subject and background

Camera settings:
Canon EOS R5, 50mm lens, f/5.6, ISO 400, shutter speed 1/125
Full depth of field — entire image sharp from foreground to background.

Color grading:
Rich warm tones, slight saturation boost in yellows and greens, natural skin tones preserved, no HDR, no overprocessing.

Focus style:
Extreme sharpness — visible skin pores, fabric fibers, hair strands, reflections in glasses, background textures, and signage details all clearly defined.

Mood:
Urban Brazilian lifestyle, confident feminine presence, editorial fashion energy, culturally rich, authentic, cinematic yet real, indistinguishable from professional photography.

items.rawPrompt:
STUDIO EDITORIAL — SINGLE SHOT v4 (DRAMATIC)


INPUT A (model image): [attach]
INPUT B (clothing image): [attach]
POSE DIRECTION: fashion portrait, Editorial body in shadow, Close-up de cima dos ombros, brincos e -30º rotação no angulo yt, voyeurism angle, jaqueta em cima do ombro, against a blue to white gradient backdrop, creating a fashion and moody atmosphere, nature light, high-contrast --profile spc2tb2


---


STEP 1 — VISUAL EXTRACTION (internal, do not output):


From INPUT A — Model:
Extract: skin tone value (light / medium / tan / deep),
skin undertone (warm / cool / neutral), body proportions,
hair color and texture, facial structure, physical build,
energy archetype (delicate / neutral / powerful / angular).


From INPUT B — Clothing:
Extract: clothing value (light / medium / dark), dominant
color temperature (warm / cool / neutral), fabric weight
and surface language (matte / glossy / washed / fluid /
structured / raw / reflective), silhouette category,
styling signals, cultural or subcultural coding of the look.


Note: if clothing is dark or highly reflective, flag this —
it will affect rim light intensity in Step 4 to ensure
separation from dark background zones.


---


STEP 2 — BACKGROUND SYSTEM (fixed, do not alter):


ENVIRONMENT: vertical three-zone linear gradient studio.
A seamless top-to-bottom gradient — black at the top,
deep crimson in the middle, near-white at the floor.
Not radial. Not circular. Not a vignette or aura.
Strictly vertical. 90° linear. Color flows downward.


EXACT COLOR VALUES — DO NOT DEVIATE:


  ZONE 1 — TOP (darkest point):
  HEX: #100808
  RGB: rgb(16, 8, 8)
  HSL: hsl(0°, 33%, 5%)
  — Near-black with the faintest warm undertone.
  — Must read as true dark, not charcoal gray.
  — Occupies approximately top 30–35% of frame.


  ZONE 2 — MIDPOINT (crimson peak):
  HEX: #8C1C1C
  RGB: rgb(140, 28, 28)
  HSL: hsl(0°, 67%, 33%)
  — Deep blood crimson. The color peaks at mid-frame
    height — roughly behind the subject's torso.
  — Not neon red. Not orange-red. Not pink-red.
  — Saturated enough to read as charged color; dark
    enough to feel dangerous, not theatrical.
  — Centered vertically at approximately 45–55% of
    frame height.


  ZONE 3 — BOTTOM (lightest point):
  HEX: #EDE5E5
  RGB: rgb(237, 229, 229)
  HSL: hsl(0°, 13%, 91%)
  — Near-white floor with the faintest warm blush.
  — Reflective, clean, minimal.
  — Occupies approximately bottom 25–30% of frame.


GRADIENT DIRECTION: top-to-bottom only. 90° linear.
Strictly vertical flow: dark → crimson → pale.
No horizontal spread. No circular emanation.
No vignette darkening at sides.
The left and right edges of the background hold
the same value as the horizontal center at any
given height — pure vertical gradient, edge to edge.


GRADIENT TRANSITION: smooth and continuous. No banding,
no hard edge between zones, no visible color break.
The black dissolves into crimson; the crimson dissolves
into near-white. Each transition is gradual.


COLOR TEMPERATURE of environment: mixed intentionally —
crimson mid-ground is warm (2800–3200K equivalent),
key light on subject is cool (5500–6200K).
This temperature conflict is structural, not accidental.


HUE LOCK: crimson zone fixed at hsl(0°). No deviation
toward magenta (H>10°), no deviation toward orange
(H<350° going warm). Pure red axis only.


PROHIBITED backgrounds:
— Radial gradient or circular color emanation
— Vignette darkening at frame edges
— Pure black flat backdrop with no gradient
— Pure white or neutral gray backdrop
— Mint, teal, or cool-toned environment
— Uniform red wash across entire background
— Gradient that reads as sunset or sky
— Visible texture, grain, or noise on backdrop
— Any sense of physical location (room, alley, wall)
— Horizontal gradient or diagonal gradient


The background must feel: vertical pressure —
darkness bearing down from above, ground dissolving
into light below, crimson heat at the center.
Architecture of weight, not decoration.


---


STEP 3 — POSE & CAMERA SELECTION (internal):


PHILOSOPHY:
The pose must feel like a decision, not a default.
Prioritize physical tension, weight, and confrontation
over elegance or symmetry. The subject dominates the frame.
Think editorial power, not commercial compliance.
The dramatic environment demands a pose that earns it —
do not place a passive body inside an active background.


If POSE DIRECTION is specified: follow it faithfully
but interpret with maximum commitment and physicality.


If free: choose the pose that makes the clothing feel
like a manifesto, not a product. Ask what posture this
environment calls for — a background this charged
requires a subject who commands it.


---


POSE REPERTOIRE — DRAMATIC EDITION:


CONFRONTATIONAL / POWER POSES:
  — Standing wide, feet planted, weight forward. Arms
    not symmetric — one extended toward camera, one
    pulled back or gripping clothing edge. Chin slightly
    down. Face into lens. Camera at hip level or below —
    shoots up. Subject becomes monumental against the
    dark upper field.
  — Crouched low, knees wide, chest forward, weight
    on the balls of feet. Both arms braced or one
    reaching toward lens. Camera at floor level,
    shooting steeply upward. Dark vignette looms
    above; crimson blooms at back. Maximum dominance.
  — Torso twist in mid-turn: body faces away, face
    turns hard back toward camera. One shoulder
    elevated. Weight shifted. Camera eye-level or
    slight low. Creates rotation energy within the frame.


FLOOR / GROUND POSES:
  — Standing, one foot planted on floor, one knee
    slightly lifted or weight shifted to one hip.
    Hands active — one at collar, one gripping waist
    or seam. Gaze direct. Camera eye-level or low.
  — Seated on floor, spine straight, one knee up,
    one leg extended. Arms framing the body — one
    on floor behind for support, one on raised knee.
    Camera slight high angle — subject reads as
    composed inside the dark field.
  — Back arched, weight on one hip, legs folded.
    Head tilted, gaze toward camera. One arm extended.
    Overhead or steep high angle — body creates strong
    graphic shape against the floor fade.


CLOSE-UP / FRAGMENT POSES:
  — Extreme close-up: face and upper chest only.
    Hard jaw angle or near-profile. One hand at
    collar, jaw, or nape. 85–105mm aesthetic.
    Background crimson bloom fills soft-focus field.
    Face sculpted by cool key against warm back-glow.
  — Mid-shot: waist to crown. Body in slight torso
    twist. Hands active — gripping, adjusting, touching.
    Direct or deliberately averted gaze with intention.
  — Fragment: thigh to crown. Clothing and face share
    frame. One hand doing something specific and visible.
    Strong rim light separates subject from dark zones.


MOVEMENT-IMPLIED POSES:
  — Mid-stride caught: one foot forward, one back.
    Arms asymmetric. Face turned mid-movement.
    Slight motion blur on non-focal elements acceptable.
  — Pivot energy: torso going one way, face going
    another. Weight visibly shifting. Dynamic freeze.
  — Hair mid-movement. Body still, hair in motion.
    Creates energy without losing clothing detail.
    Works especially well against the radial bloom.


CAMERA ANGLE — EXPANDED:
  — Ultra-low (floor level, shooting steeply up):
    for crouched or confrontational power poses.
    Dark upper field becomes ceiling pressure.
    Subject is monumental. Most effective angle
    for this environment.
  — Low angle (below hip, shooting up): standard
    power framing. Crimson bloom centers behind torso.
  — Eye level neutral: mid and torso poses.
  — Slight high angle (just above eye, down): floor
    poses and arched compositions.
  — Pushed-in with slight wide distortion (35–50mm):
    confrontational close-ups — face and upper body
    only. Never full body at wide angle.


Camera angle must amplify the pose's intention AND
the environment's charge. Ask: does this angle activate
the dark field above and the crimson bloom behind?


---


STEP 4 — FINAL IMAGE OUTPUT:


Generate a single, high-resolution dramatic editorial
photograph. One pose. One frame. Not a grid. Not a
composite. Not a contact sheet.


SUBJECT: exact model from INPUT A wearing exact garments
from INPUT B. Preserve all of: skin tone, face, body
proportions, hair, and every clothing detail — color,
texture, stitching, hardware, logo placement.


POSE: as selected in Step 3. Committed, intentional,
physical. Not neutral, not catalog. The subject has
presence — the pose commands the space.


BACKGROUND: as defined in Step 2. Dark radial field
with crimson bloom at center-back, fading to near-white
at floor. No props, no furniture, no texture on
backdrop surface.


FORMAT: portrait orientation (4:5 or 2:3 preferred).
Full bleed. No border, no text, no watermark, no frame.


LIGHTING SYSTEM — EXTREME CHIAROSCURO:


  SHADOW PHILOSOPHY:
  The shadow is not an absence of light — it is a
  presence. Shadows must be deep, intentional, and
  compositionally active. The unlit side of the subject
  approaches true black. This is not correctable. Do not
  fill. Do not soften. Embrace the dark.
  Target overall contrast ratio: 1:6 to 1:10.


  KEY LIGHT:
  — Color temperature: cool-neutral (5500–6200K).
  — Position: hard side light or 3/4 front, 60–90°
    from camera axis. Elevated 20–40° above subject.
  — Quality: hard to semi-hard source. NOT a softbox.
    NOT diffused. Hard light creates defined shadow edges
    on facial planes, collarbones, shoulders, fabric folds.
  — The light falls across the subject like a blade —
    one side fully lit, one side fully dark.
  — On the face: cheekbone, brow ridge, jaw, and nose
    bridge must show hard shadow casting. Rembrandt or
    split lighting pattern. Not beauty lighting.
  — On the body: every structural plane — shoulder cap,
    pectoral edge, hip crest, fabric seam — must cast
    a visible shadow onto the adjacent surface.


  FILL LIGHT:
  — Zero to near-zero. Maximum ratio key:fill = 1:8.
  — Shadow side must hold near-black (#0A0A0A range).
  — If any fill exists at all, it is purely ambient —
    the faint reflected light from the pale floor,
    not a deliberate fill source.
  — NO reflectors. NO bounce cards. NO softbox fill.
    The dark side stays dark.


  RIM / SEPARATION LIGHT:
  — Strong, positioned opposite the key at 140–170°.
  — Purpose: cuts the subject's silhouette out of the
    dark upper zone of the background.
  — Color: cool or with very faint crimson contamination
    from background gel spill. Never pure white.
  — Must trace the full edge of the subject: shoulder,
    arm, hip, outer leg — a precise light contour.
  — On dark garments: this rim is critical. It is the
    only thing separating dark fabric from dark
    background. It must be bright enough to define
    every edge of the silhouette.


  BACKGROUND LIGHT / GEL:
  — Source aimed at backdrop only, not at subject.
  — Color: deep crimson matching Zone 2 HEX (#8C1C1C).
  — Position: mid-height behind subject, aimed at
    the background wall/seamless paper.
  — Creates the warm vertical glow in the background.
  — Minimal spill onto subject — only faint warm
    contamination on the very edges of hair or
    outermost garment surfaces is acceptable.


  SHADOW EDGES:
  — Hard light means hard shadow edges on the subject.
  — Transitions from highlight to shadow on skin: sharp,
    not gradual. The terminator line is defined.
  — Exception: very slight edge softening acceptable on
    skin surfaces curved away from light (forehead,
    shoulder cap) — but never on jaw, cheekbone, nose.


  COLOR TEMPERATURE CONFLICT — STRUCTURAL:
  — Subject lit in cool precision (key light, 5500–6200K).
  — Background glows in warm crimson (background gel).
  — This contrast is never neutralized. Do not correct
    the mixed temperature. The cool subject against the
    warm environment is the image's core tension.


QUALITY MARKERS:
— Realistic skin micro-texture, pores, natural moisture,
  subsurface scattering. No airbrushing, no smoothing.
— Faithful fabric reproduction: satin sheen, leather
  grain, sequin scatter, denim weave, latex mirror —
  exactly as in INPUT B. No color shift, no detail loss.
  Dark fabrics must retain material identity even
  against the dark background — rim light ensures this.
— Natural hair texture and movement from INPUT A.
— Clothing fits and drapes realistically on the body.
— Gaze: direct, semi-direct, or deliberately averted
  with intention. Never commercial catalog expression.
  Attitude, power, and interiority — not pleasantness.
— Hands and feet in frame must be anatomically precise.


CAMERA: 85mm lens aesthetic as default. 35–50mm only
for pushed-in confrontational close-ups. Depth of field
calibrated to pose: shallow for close-up fragments,
medium-deep for full body. Subtle natural grain.
No over-sharpening, no fake HDR, no preset color grading.


AESTHETIC REFERENCE: Dazed & Confused, Numero, i-D,
Alexander McQueen editorial campaigns, Nick Knight
photography, Thierry Mugler archive imagery.
Operatic but precise. Bodily and charged.
Glamour with danger underneath.
Not commercial. Not catalog. Not influencer.


---


STRICT NEGATIVES:
multiple panels, composite grid, flat lay, mannequin,
pure black flat backdrop, pure white backdrop, neutral
gray backdrop, mint or cool-toned environment, sunset
or warm landscape gradient, any readable physical location
or set, theatrical stage feeling, concert lighting look,
altered face or skin tone, changed body proportions,
changed clothing colors or textures, logo modification,
airbrushed skin, plastic finish, 3D render feel, cartoon
aesthetic, neon glow, fake HDR, ring-light halo, catalog
pose, commercial retail expression, forced smile,
oversaturated background, uniform background illumination,
visible backdrop seam or horizon line, watermark, text
overlay, lifeless neutral standing pose, symmetric
arms-at-sides stance, hidden or invisible hands,
dead gaze, flat frontal camera with no intention,
cool background behind warm-lit subject (temperature
conflict must always favor warm bg / cool subject),
subject fully merging with dark field (rim separation
is mandatory).

No vignette darkening at sides.
The left and right edges of the background hold
the same value as the horizontal center at any
given height — pure vertical gradient, edge to edge.


GRADIENT TRANSITION: smooth and continuous. No banding,
no hard edge between zones, no visible color break.
The black dissolves into crimson; the crimson dissolves
into near-white. Each transition is gradual.


COLOR TEMPERATURE of environment: mixed intentionally —
crimson mid-ground is warm (2800–3200K equivalent),
key light on subject is cool (5500–6200K).
This temperature conflict is structural, not accidental.


HUE LOCK: crimson zone fixed at hsl(0°). No deviation
toward magenta (H>10°), no deviation toward orange
(H<350° going warm). Pure red axis only.


PROHIBITED backgrounds:
— Radial gradient or circular color emanation
— Vignette darkening at frame edges
— Pure black flat backdrop with no gradient
— Pure white or neutral gray backdrop
— Mint, teal, or cool-toned environment
— Uniform red wash across entire background
— Gradient that reads as sunset or sky
— Visible texture, grain, or noise on backdrop
— Any sense of physical location (room, alley, wall)
— Horizontal gradient or diagonal gradient


The background must feel: vertical pressure —
darkness bearing down from above, ground dissolving
into light below, crimson heat at the center.
Architecture of weight, not decoration.


---


STEP 3 — POSE & CAMERA SELECTION (internal):


PHILOSOPHY:
The pose must feel like a decision, not a default.
Prioritize physical tension, weight, and confrontation
over elegance or symmetry. The subject dominates the frame.
Think editorial power, not commercial compliance.
The dramatic environment demands a pose that earns it —
do not place a passive body inside an active background.


If POSE DIRECTION is specified: follow it faithfully
but interpret with maximum commitment and physicality.


If free: choose the pose that makes the clothing feel
like a manifesto, not a product. Ask what posture this
environment calls for — a background this charged
requires a subject who commands it.


---


POSE REPERTOIRE — DRAMATIC EDITION:


CONFRONTATIONAL / POWER POSES:
  — Standing wide, feet planted, weight forward. Arms
    not symmetric — one extended toward camera, one
    pulled back or gripping clothing edge. Chin slightly
    down. Face into lens. Camera at hip level or below —
    shoots up. Subject becomes monumental against the
    dark upper field.
  — Crouched low, knees wide, chest forward, weight
    on the balls of feet. Both arms braced or one
    reaching toward lens. Camera at floor level,
    shooting steeply upward. Dark vignette looms
    above; crimson blooms at back. Maximum dominance.
  — Torso twist in mid-turn: body faces away, face
    turns hard back toward camera. One shoulder
    elevated. Weight shifted. Camera eye-level or
    slight low. Creates rotation energy within the frame.


FLOOR / GROUND POSES:
  — Standing, one foot planted on floor, one knee
    slightly lifted or weight shifted to one hip.
    Hands active — one at collar, one gripping waist
    or seam. Gaze direct. Camera eye-level or low.
  — Seated on floor, spine straight, one knee up,
    one leg extended. Arms framing the body — one
    on floor behind for support, one on raised knee.
    Camera slight high angle — subject reads as
    composed inside the dark field.
  — Back arched, weight on one hip, legs folded.
    Head tilted, gaze toward camera. One arm extended.
    Overhead or steep high angle — body creates strong
    graphic shape against the floor fade.


CLOSE-UP / FRAGMENT POSES:
  — Extreme close-up: face and upper chest only.
    Hard jaw angle or near-profile. One hand at
    collar, jaw, or nape. 85–105mm aesthetic.
    Background crimson bloom fills soft-focus field.
    Face sculpted by cool key against warm back-glow.
  — Mid-shot: waist to crown. Body in slight torso
    twist. Hands active — gripping, adjusting, touching.
    Direct or deliberately averted gaze with intention.
  — Fragment: thigh to crown. Clothing and face share
    frame. One hand doing something specific and visible.
    Strong rim light separates subject from dark zones.


MOVEMENT-IMPLIED POSES:
  — Mid-stride caught: one foot forward, one back.
    Arms asymmetric. Face turned mid-movement.
    Slight motion blur on non-focal elements acceptable.
  — Pivot energy: torso going one way, face going
    another. Weight visibly shifting. Dynamic freeze.
  — Hair mid-movement. Body still, hair in motion.
    Creates energy without losing clothing detail.
    Works especially well against the radial bloom.


CAMERA ANGLE — EXPANDED:
  — Ultra-low (floor level, shooting steeply up):
    for crouched or confrontational power poses.
    Dark upper field becomes ceiling pressure.
    Subject is monumental. Most effective angle
    for this environment.
  — Low angle (below hip, shooting up): standard
    power framing. Crimson bloom centers behind torso.
  — Eye level neutral: mid and torso poses.
  — Slight high angle (just above eye, down): floor
    poses and arched compositions.
  — Pushed-in with slight wide distortion (35–50mm):
    confrontational close-ups — face and upper body
    only. Never full body at wide angle.


Camera angle must amplify the pose's intention AND
the environment's charge. Ask: does this angle activate
the dark field above and the crimson bloom behind?


---


STEP 4 — FINAL IMAGE OUTPUT:


Generate a single, high-resolution dramatic editorial
photograph. One pose. One frame. Not a grid. Not a
composite. Not a contact sheet.


SUBJECT: exact model from INPUT A wearing exact garments
from INPUT B. Preserve all of: skin tone, face, body
proportions, hair, and every clothing detail — color,
texture, stitching, hardware, logo placement.


POSE: as selected in Step 3. Committed, intentional,
physical. Not neutral, not catalog. The subject has
presence — the pose commands the space.


BACKGROUND: as defined in Step 2. Dark radial field
with crimson bloom at center-back, fading to near-white
at floor. No props, no furniture, no texture on
backdrop surface.


FORMAT: portrait orientation (4:5 or 2:3 preferred).
Full bleed. No border, no text, no watermark, no frame.


LIGHTING SYSTEM — EXTREME CHIAROSCURO:


  SHADOW PHILOSOPHY:
  The shadow is not an absence of light — it is a
  presence. Shadows must be deep, intentional, and
  compositionally active. The unlit side of the subject
  approaches true black. This is not correctable. Do not
  fill. Do not soften. Embrace the dark.
  Target overall contrast ratio: 1:6 to 1:10.


  KEY LIGHT:
  — Color temperature: cool-neutral (5500–6200K).
  — Position: hard side light or 3/4 front, 60–90°
    from camera axis. Elevated 20–40° above subject.
  — Quality: hard to semi-hard source. NOT a softbox.
    NOT diffused. Hard light creates defined shadow edges
    on facial planes, collarbones, shoulders, fabric folds.
  — The light falls across the subject like a blade —
    one side fully lit, one side fully dark.
  — On the face: cheekbone, brow ridge, jaw, and nose
    bridge must show hard shadow casting. Rembrandt or
    split lighting pattern. Not beauty lighting.
  — On the body: every structural plane — shoulder cap,
    pectoral edge, hip crest, fabric seam — must cast
    a visible shadow onto the adjacent surface.


  FILL LIGHT:
  — Zero to near-zero. Maximum ratio key:fill = 1:8.
  — Shadow side must hold near-black (#0A0A0A range).
  — If any fill exists at all, it is purely ambient —
    the faint reflected light from the pale floor,
    not a deliberate fill source.
  — NO reflectors. NO bounce cards. NO softbox fill.
    The dark side stays dark.


  RIM / SEPARATION LIGHT:
  — Strong, positioned opposite the key at 140–170°.
  — Purpose: cuts the subject's silhouette out of the
    dark upper zone of the background.
  — Color: cool or with very faint crimson contamination
    from background gel spill. Never pure white.
  — Must trace the full edge of the subject: shoulder,
    arm, hip, outer leg — a precise light contour.
  — On dark garments: this rim is critical. It is the
    only thing separating dark fabric from dark
    background. It must be bright enough to define
    every edge of the silhouette.


  BACKGROUND LIGHT / GEL:
  — Source aimed at backdrop only, not at subject.
  — Color: deep crimson matching Zone 2 HEX (#8C1C1C).
  — Position: mid-height behind subject, aimed at
    the background wall/seamless paper.
  — Creates the warm vertical glow in the background.
  — Minimal spill onto subject — only faint warm
    contamination on the very edges of hair or
    outermost garment surfaces is acceptable.


  SHADOW EDGES:
  — Hard light means hard shadow edges on the subject.
  — Transitions from highlight to shadow on skin: sharp,
    not gradual. The terminator line is defined.
  — Exception: very slight edge softening acceptable on
    skin surfaces curved away from light (forehead,
    shoulder cap) — but never on jaw, cheekbone, nose.


  COLOR TEMPERATURE CONFLICT — STRUCTURAL:
  — Subject lit in cool precision (key light, 5500–6200K).
  — Background glows in warm crimson (background gel).
  — This contrast is never neutralized. Do not correct
    the mixed temperature. The cool subject against the
    warm environment is the image's core tension.


QUALITY MARKERS:
— Realistic skin micro-texture, pores, natural moisture,
  subsurface scattering. No airbrushing, no smoothing.
— Faithful fabric reproduction: satin sheen, leather
  grain, sequin scatter, denim weave, latex mirror —
  exactly as in INPUT B. No color shift, no detail loss.
  Dark fabrics must retain material identity even
  against the dark background — rim light ensures this.
— Natural hair texture and movement from INPUT A.
— Clothing fits and drapes realistically on the body.
— Gaze: direct, semi-direct, or deliberately averted
  with intention. Never commercial catalog expression.
  Attitude, power, and interiority — not pleasantness.
— Hands and feet in frame must be anatomically precise.


CAMERA: 85mm lens aesthetic as default. 35–50mm only
for pushed-in confrontational close-ups. Depth of field
calibrated to pose: shallow for close-up fragments,
medium-deep for full body. Subtle natural grain.
No over-sharpening, no fake HDR, no preset color grading.


AESTHETIC REFERENCE: Dazed & Confused, Numero, i-D,
Alexander McQueen editorial campaigns, Nick Knight
photography, Thierry Mugler archive imagery.
Operatic but precise. Bodily and charged.
Glamour with danger underneath.
Not commercial. Not catalog. Not influencer.


---


STRICT NEGATIVES:
multiple panels, composite grid, flat lay, mannequin,
pure black flat backdrop, pure white backdrop, neutral
gray backdrop, mint or cool-toned environment, sunset
or warm landscape gradient, any readable physical location
or set, theatrical stage feeling, concert lighting look,
altered face or skin tone, changed body proportions,
changed clothing colors or textures, logo modification,
airbrushed skin, plastic finish, 3D render feel, cartoon
aesthetic, neon glow, fake HDR, ring-light halo, catalog
pose, commercial retail expression, forced smile,
oversaturated background, uniform background illumination,
visible backdrop seam or horizon line, watermark, text
overlay, lifeless neutral standing pose, symmetric
arms-at-sides stance, hidden or invisible hands,
dead gaze, flat frontal camera with no intention,
cool background behind warm-lit subject (temperature
conflict must always favor warm bg / cool subject),
subject fully merging with dark field (rim separation
is mandatory).

items.rawPrompt:
EDITORIAL CONCEPT: High-end fashion editorial portrait focusing on sensory intimacy, classic European summer warmth, and elegant nonchalance. The image balances a high-fashion mood with raw, organic elements, establishing a soft and inviting narrative through natural poses and interaction with fruit.

SUBJECT INITIAL IDENTITY & CHARACTER CONSISTENCY: A beautiful young Caucasian woman with striking green-blue eyes, symmetrical facial bone structure, defined jawline, and natural full lips with a soft dusty rose matte lipstick. Her hair is voluminous, styled in effortless,, with loose strands framing her face.

EXPRESSION & POSE: The subject is captured from the chest up, her head slightly tilted upward and looking away to the upper right corner in a pensive, dreamy, and nostalgic gaze. Her right hand is brought up to her face, delicately resting a ripe, textured peach against her chin. Her left hand is positioned lower in the frame, cradling another fresh peach, creating a balanced vertical composition.

WARDROBE & ACCESSORIES: She wears an elegant, cream-white silk slip dress with intricate ivory lace embroidery detailing along the deep V-neckline. On her right wrist, she wears a chunky, smooth, organic-shaped matte white resin or ceramic bangle. On her left wrist, a wide, polished reflective yellow gold cuff bracelet is visible.

ENVIRONMENT & SCENOGRAPHY: The background is a dimly lit, rustic yet sophisticated Mediterranean villa interior. An antique dark wood framed mirror or doorway is softly blurred in the background to the left, adding historical depth without creating visual clutter. The atmosphere is quiet, serene, and warm.

LIGHTING DESIGN: Soft, directional natural light streams in from a large window on the right side of the frame, acting as a gentle key light that illuminates the subject's face, highlighting her skin texture and the golden highlights of her hair. A subtle, warm rim light separates her silhouette from the deep, shadow-toned background.

CAMERA ARCHITECTURE & TECHNICAL SPECS: Shot on a Leica M11 Rangefinder camera with a Leica Noctilux-M 50mm f/1.2 ASPH lens. Aperture is set to f/1.8 to achieve a shallow depth of field with a smooth fall-off. Shutter speed: 1/160s. ISO: 200 to maximize dynamic range and maintain clean shadows.

WHITE BALANCE CONFIGURATION: Custom Daylight White Balance set to 5600K with a subtle +3 tint toward Magenta to enrich the warm, creamy undertones of the dress, the golden hair, and the organic red-orange hues of the peaches, while keeping the skin tones lifelike.

MICRO-TEXTURES & FIDELITY: Exceptional micro-details are preserved throughout the image. Individual strands of hair, fine pores on the skin, and the velvety fuzz and organic imperfections on the skin of the peaches are sharply defined. The delicate weave of the lace and the smooth texture of the silk dress show realistic micro-folds and fabric grains. High contrast, warm filmic color grading with zero digital airbrushing.

Subtle particle nodes and floating vertex points drift just above the surface like suspended data points. items.rawPrompt:
STUDIO EDITORIAL — DUAL SUBJECT / SINGLE SHOT v1 (SAME GARMENT)
INPUT A (model 1 image): [attach]
INPUT B (model 2 image): [attach]
INPUT C (clothing — both models): [attach]

STEP 1 — VISUAL EXTRACTION (internal, do not output):
From INPUT A — Model 1:
Extract: skin tone value (light / medium / tan / deep),
skin undertone (warm / cool / neutral), body proportions,
hair color and texture, facial structure, estimated height
and frame relative to model 2.
From INPUT B — Model 2:
Extract: skin tone value, skin undertone, body proportions,
hair color and texture, facial structure, estimated height
and frame relative to model 1.
CONTRAST RULE: identify the primary visual contrast
between the two subjects — tone, height, hair, or build.
This contrast must be legible and preserved in the final
image. Do not average or blend any physical features
between subjects. Each model must remain individually
identifiable and true to her input.
From INPUT C — Clothing (both models):
Extract: clothing value (light / medium / dark), dominant
color temperature (warm / cool / neutral), fabric weight
and surface language (matte, glossy, washed, fluid,
structured, raw), silhouette category, styling signals.
SAME-GARMENT RULE: both subjects wear identical garments
from INPUT C. The garment must drape, fit, and behave
realistically on each individual body — proportions,
tension points, and fabric behavior will differ between
subjects according to their individual body structure.
Do not force an identical fit. Identical garment,
individual drape.
WARDROBE HARMONY CHECK: since both subjects wear the
same garment, the compositional relationship in STEP 3
must create sufficient visual differentiation through
pose, body angle, and spatial offset — the clothing
itself will not provide contrast between subjects.

STEP 2 — BACKGROUND SELECTION (internal):
FIXED: seamless warm off-white infinity curve.
No texture on backdrop. Floor and wall are one unbroken
continuous surface. No horizon line visible.
Lighting must be consistent across both subjects —
neutral white balance 5500K. Key light simulates a single
large soft-box source at 30–45° to the frame, creating
coherent shadow logic across both bodies.
No subject should be lit differently from the other
unless the pose places one naturally in partial shadow —
in which case shadow fall-off must feel intentional,
not accidental.
Rim or separation light acceptable and encouraged —
both subjects must read clearly and independently
against the off-white field.

STEP 3 — POSE & COMPOSITION (internal):
PHILOSOPHY — TWO SUBJECTS:
The dynamic between two subjects is a relationship,
not a duplication. Avoid mirroring at all costs.
One subject leads — the other responds or diverges.
Silhouettes must read as two distinct graphic shapes
that coexist without merging.
SPATIAL LOGIC — choose one:
OPTION A — DEPTH OFFSET:
One subject placed closer to camera in slight foreground,
the other behind and laterally offset. Bodies angled
toward the same direction or slightly toward each other.
Creates depth and avoids flat, side-by-side symmetry.
Camera: eye level to slight low angle.
OPTION B — BACK TO BACK:
Subjects standing back-to-back, bodies touching or
nearly touching. One faces camera directly, one faces
away or 3/4 away. Gazes diverge — one into lens,
one off-frame. Strong graphic silhouette read.
Camera: eye level, medium shot waist-up or full body.
OPTION C — VERTICAL SPLIT:
One subject standing, one crouched, seated, or on
floor beside her. Vertical contrast in height creates
compositional tension. Both facing camera but at
different angles. One gaze direct, one averted.
Camera: eye level or slight low angle to honor
the standing figure.
OPTION D — ASYMMETRIC FACING:
Subjects facing each other but not symmetrically —
one turned more toward camera, one more in profile.
Bodies close but not touching. Tension in the space
between them. Gazes: one toward camera, one toward
the other subject.
Camera: 3/4 angle to the pair, not straight-on.
GAZE RULE (mandatory):
Gazes must never mirror each other.
— If Model 1 looks into lens: Model 2 looks away,
downward, or toward Model 1.
— If both gaze away: they must gaze in different
directions.
— Direct double gaze into lens is permitted only
if the pose creates enough asymmetry elsewhere
(body angle, arm position, height differential)
to prevent a symmetrical, catalog-style read.
ARM AND HAND RULE (mandatory):
Arms must not mirror each other across subjects.
If Model 1 has one arm raised, Model 2's arms
should be neutral, lowered, or differently active.
Hands must be visible for at least one subject.
Hands must be anatomically precise — no hidden
or ambiguous hand placement.
ATTITUDE RULE:
The two subjects do not need to relate narratively.
They may exist in the same frame without acknowledging
each other. The image is about coexistence of presence,
not a story between characters. No forced interaction,
no theatrical staging.

STEP 4 — FINAL IMAGE OUTPUT:
Generate a single, high-resolution studio editorial
photograph. One frame. Two subjects. Not a grid.
Not a composite diptych. Not a contact sheet.
Both subjects must appear within a single continuous image.
SUBJECT 1: exact model from INPUT A wearing exact garments
from INPUT C. Preserve all of: skin tone, face, body
proportions, hair, and every clothing detail — color,
texture, stitching, hardware, logo placement.
SUBJECT 2: exact model from INPUT B wearing the same
garments from INPUT C. Same preservation rules as Subject 1.
Clothing must read as identical in design and colorway
to Subject 1's garment, while adapting naturally to
Subject 2's individual body proportions and frame.
IDENTITY INTEGRITY: both models must remain individually
recognizable and true to their input images. Do not blend
facial features, do not alter skin tones, do not average
body proportions. Each is a distinct individual wearing
the same garment differently.
POSE: as selected in Step 3. Asymmetric, intentional,
editorial. Not catalog, not commercial, not forced
interaction. Two presences sharing a frame.
BACKGROUND: seamless warm off-white infinity curve.
No props, no furniture, no texture on backdrop.
FORMAT: portrait orientation preferred (4:5 or 2:3).
If spatial relationship demands wider framing,
landscape (3:2) is acceptable. Full bleed.
No border, no text, no watermark, no frame.
LIGHTING: single coherent soft-box light source at
30–45°, fill ratio 1:2 to 1:3, consistent across
both subjects. Shadow logic must be physically coherent —
both figures lit from the same source direction.
Neutral white balance 5500K. No colored gels.
Rim or separation light acceptable on both or either
subject where necessary to prevent merging with
the off-white backdrop.
QUALITY MARKERS:
— Realistic skin micro-texture on both subjects:
pores, natural moisture, subsurface scattering.
No airbrushing, no smoothing.
— Faithful fabric reproduction for both: exact color,
texture, drape, weight, finish from INPUT C.
No color shift, no detail loss. The garment must
read as the same piece on two different bodies —
not two similar garments, not two styled variations.
— Natural hair texture and movement for each model
individually — do not homogenize hair quality.
— Clothing fits and drapes realistically on each
individual body — fabric tension, silhouette, and
fall will differ naturally between subjects.
— Gaze: direct, semi-direct, or deliberately averted
with intention — following GAZE RULE above.
Never commercial-catalog expression, never forced smile.
— Hands and feet in frame must be anatomically precise
for both subjects.
CAMERA: 85mm lens aesthetic as default for full-body
and mid-body shots. 50mm if spatial relationship
requires wider coverage of two figures. Depth of field
calibrated to ensure both subjects are in acceptable
focus — avoid shallow DoF that renders one figure
blurry unless foreground/background depth separation
is intentional and compositionally justified.
Subtle natural grain. No over-sharpening, no fake HDR,
no preset color grading.
AESTHETIC REFERENCE: Vogue Italia, System Magazine,
Acne Paper, i-D, CR Fashion Book.
Restrained but charged. Precise and bodily.
Not commercial. Not catalog. Not influencer.
Not a friendship photo. Not a campaign smile.

STRICT NEGATIVES:
multiple panels, composite grid, flat lay, mannequin,
diptych format, pure white #fff backdrop,
black backdrop, chromatic colored backdrop,
mirrored or symmetric poses between subjects,
identical gaze direction on both models,
merged or blended silhouettes,
averaged or blended facial features between subjects,
altered skin tone on either model,
changed body proportions on either model,
changed clothing colors or textures from INPUT C,
logo modification, airbrushed skin, plastic finish,
3D render feel, cartoon aesthetic, neon glow,
fake HDR, ring-light halo, catalog pose,
commercial retail expression, forced smile,
forced narrative interaction between subjects,
oversaturated, heavy vignette, watermark,
text overlay, symmetrical mirrored composition,
hands invisible or hidden on both subjects,
dead or vacant gaze on both subjects simultaneously,
straight-on flat camera angle with no intention,
one subject visually erasing or dominating the other
to the point of illegibility,
garments rendered as two different pieces or colorways,
forced identical fit ignoring individual body structure.

not a duplication. Avoid mirroring at all costs.
One subject leads — the other responds or diverges.
Silhouettes must read as two distinct graphic shapes
that coexist without merging.
SPATIAL LOGIC — choose one:
OPTION A — DEPTH OFFSET:
One subject placed closer to camera in slight foreground,
the other behind and laterally offset. Bodies angled
toward the same direction or slightly toward each other.
Creates depth and avoids flat, side-by-side symmetry.
Camera: eye level to slight low angle.
OPTION B — BACK TO BACK:
Subjects standing back-to-back, bodies touching or
nearly touching. One faces camera directly, one faces
away or 3/4 away. Gazes diverge — one into lens,
one off-frame. Strong graphic silhouette read.
Camera: eye level, medium shot waist-up or full body.
OPTION C — VERTICAL SPLIT:
One subject standing, one crouched, seated, or on
floor beside her. Vertical contrast in height creates
compositional tension. Both facing camera but at
different angles. One gaze direct, one averted.
Camera: eye level or slight low angle to honor
the standing figure.
OPTION D — ASYMMETRIC FACING:
Subjects facing each other but not symmetrically —
one turned more toward camera, one more in profile.
Bodies close but not touching. Tension in the space
between them. Gazes: one toward camera, one toward
the other subject.
Camera: 3/4 angle to the pair, not straight-on.
GAZE RULE (mandatory):
Gazes must never mirror each other.
— If Model 1 looks into lens: Model 2 looks away,
downward, or toward Model 1.
— If both gaze away: they must gaze in different
directions.
— Direct double gaze into lens is permitted only
if the pose creates enough asymmetry elsewhere
(body angle, arm position, height differential)
to prevent a symmetrical, catalog-style read.
ARM AND HAND RULE (mandatory):
Arms must not mirror each other across subjects.
If Model 1 has one arm raised, Model 2's arms
should be neutral, lowered, or differently active.
Hands must be visible for at least one subject.
Hands must be anatomically precise — no hidden
or ambiguous hand placement.
ATTITUDE RULE:
The two subjects do not need to relate narratively.
They may exist in the same frame without acknowledging
each other. The image is about coexistence of presence,
not a story between characters. No forced interaction,
no theatrical staging.

STEP 4 — FINAL IMAGE OUTPUT:
Generate a single, high-resolution studio editorial
photograph. One frame. Two subjects. Not a grid.
Not a composite diptych. Not a contact sheet.
Both subjects must appear within a single continuous image.
SUBJECT 1: exact model from INPUT A wearing exact garments
from INPUT C. Preserve all of: skin tone, face, body
proportions, hair, and every clothing detail — color,
texture, stitching, hardware, logo placement.
SUBJECT 2: exact model from INPUT B wearing the same
garments from INPUT C. Same preservation rules as Subject 1.
Clothing must read as identical in design and colorway
to Subject 1's garment, while adapting naturally to
Subject 2's individual body proportions and frame.
IDENTITY INTEGRITY: both models must remain individually
recognizable and true to their input images. Do not blend
facial features, do not alter skin tones, do not average
body proportions. Each is a distinct individual wearing
the same garment differently.
POSE: as selected in Step 3. Asymmetric, intentional,
editorial. Not catalog, not commercial, not forced
interaction. Two presences sharing a frame.
BACKGROUND: seamless warm off-white infinity curve.
No props, no furniture, no texture on backdrop.
FORMAT: portrait orientation preferred (4:5 or 2:3).
If spatial relationship demands wider framing,
landscape (3:2) is acceptable. Full bleed.
No border, no text, no watermark, no frame.
LIGHTING: single coherent soft-box light source at
30–45°, fill ratio 1:2 to 1:3, consistent across
both subjects. Shadow logic must be physically coherent —
both figures lit from the same source direction.
Neutral white balance 5500K. No colored gels.
Rim or separation light acceptable on both or either
subject where necessary to prevent merging with
the off-white backdrop.
QUALITY MARKERS:
— Realistic skin micro-texture on both subjects:
pores, natural moisture, subsurface scattering.
No airbrushing, no smoothing.
— Faithful fabric reproduction for both: exact color,
texture, drape, weight, finish from INPUT C.
No color shift, no detail loss. The garment must
read as the same piece on two different bodies —
not two similar garments, not two styled variations.
— Natural hair texture and movement for each model
individually — do not homogenize hair quality.
— Clothing fits and drapes realistically on each
individual body — fabric tension, silhouette, and
fall will differ naturally between subjects.
— Gaze: direct, semi-direct, or deliberately averted
with intention — following GAZE RULE above.
Never commercial-catalog expression, never forced smile.
— Hands and feet in frame must be anatomically precise
for both subjects.
CAMERA: 85mm lens aesthetic as default for full-body
and mid-body shots. 50mm if spatial relationship
requires wider coverage of two figures. Depth of field
calibrated to ensure both subjects are in acceptable
focus — avoid shallow DoF that renders one figure
blurry unless foreground/background depth separation
is intentional and compositionally justified.
Subtle natural grain. No over-sharpening, no fake HDR,
no preset color grading.
AESTHETIC REFERENCE: Vogue Italia, System Magazine,
Acne Paper, i-D, CR Fashion Book.
Restrained but charged. Precise and bodily.
Not commercial. Not catalog. Not influencer.
Not a friendship photo. Not a campaign smile.

STRICT NEGATIVES:
multiple panels, composite grid, flat lay, mannequin,
diptych format, pure white #fff backdrop,
black backdrop, chromatic colored backdrop,
mirrored or symmetric poses between subjects,
identical gaze direction on both models,
merged or blended silhouettes,
averaged or blended facial features between subjects,
altered skin tone on either model,
changed body proportions on either model,
changed clothing colors or textures from INPUT C,
logo modification, airbrushed skin, plastic finish,
3D render feel, cartoon aesthetic, neon glow,
fake HDR, ring-light halo, catalog pose,
commercial retail expression, forced smile,
forced narrative interaction between subjects,
oversaturated, heavy vignette, watermark,
text overlay, symmetrical mirrored composition,
hands invisible or hidden on both subjects,
dead or vacant gaze on both subjects simultaneously,
straight-on flat camera angle with no intention,
one subject visually erasing or dominating the other
to the point of illegibility,
garments rendered as two different pieces or colorways,
forced identical fit ignoring individual body structure.

items.rawPrompt:
Shot from just above the material surface, low Dutch angle 
12° tilt clockwise, vintage cinematic action photography 
aesthetic, Pentax 67 with SMC 400mm f/4 ED telephoto, 
Kodak Ektar 100 rated at box speed — no push, 
the saturation is already implicit in the material.
Shutter: 1/4000s. The freeze is absolute.

A surfer — male, lean, body coiled low into a 
committed full-rail carving turn — rides the 
inner face of a wave that has broken the terms 
of its own material. The wave is urushi lacquer: 
deep crimson-black at its base, dense and non-aqueous, 
carrying gold veins through its mass the way 
kintsugi carries repair. But at the crest — 
at the exact point of breaking — the lacquer 
shatters. The lip explodes not into foam but into 
white lacquer shards and gold-dust spray, 
erupting upward and backward against the cobalt sky 
in a plume that reads simultaneously as surf 
and as a thing being destroyed. The backlight 
catches this eruption from behind the crest: 
a brilliant amber-gold halo burns through the 
fragmenting material at the top of the wave, 
the only warm light source in the frame — 
not a sun, but the wave's own interior 
releasing itself at the breaking point.

The surfer's suit: a single-piece deep slate-teal 
latex, wet-sheen — the color sits between 
the wave's shadow valleys and the cobalt sky, 
belonging fully to neither. Where his body 
tilts into the lacquer wall, the suit's surface 
reflects the crimson back at a slightly cooler tone, 
creating a chromatic interference at the contact edge. 
His right arm trails, fingers drawn along the wave face. 
The contact point does not splash. It leaves a line — 
a mark in the lacquer surface, briefly legible, 
immediately closing behind him as the material 
reasserts its own continuity.

The foreground: a plane of large, suspended 
gold-tinted spheres — convex, mercury-like — 
occupying the near distance between lens and rider. 
These are not water droplets rendered as bokeh. 
They are the wave's material logic crystallized 
mid-air: perfectly circular at their perimeter, 
refracting the amber backlight through their volume, 
each one a compressed image of the entire scene 
inverted inside itself. They drift at 1/4000s 
frozen in their drift — not falling, 
not arriving, simply occupying the foreground 
as a semi-transparent interference field 
through which the surfer must be perceived.

Telephoto compression at 400mm collapses depth: 
the erupting white-gold crest, the rider, 
and the mercury foreground plane are pressed 
into the same focal slab. The cobalt sky 
visible above the wave's broken lip is a fragment, 
a sliver — absolute, ungraded, zero atmosphere.

COLOR PALETTE 60/30/10:
60% — deep crimson-lacquer black (#4A0F0F / #5C1515) 
as the wave's main body — opaque in its valleys, 
mirror-reflective at its convex ridges, 
absolute in its shadows. Lifted blacks only 
where the vintage film grain softens 
the deepest compression zones — not as aesthetic, 
as material limit.
30% — fractured gold and tarnished amber 
(#C8922A / #A67820 / #E8C96A at the halo peak) — 
vein structure in the wave, the backlit eruption 
at the crest, and the mercury-sphere foreground 
catching warm interior light.
10% — deep slate-teal (#2E4F5A) and cobalt sky 
fragment (#0D2B6B) — the surfer's suit 
and the only cool counterweight 
against the wave's thermal logic.

LIGHTING:
Primary source: backlighting through the breaking 
lacquer crest — amber-gold, diffuse, creating 
a halo effect at the top of the wave as the 
material shatters and becomes translucent 
at its thinnest point. No sun disc. No fill. 
The rider is lit by this single transmitted 
warm source from above-behind, 
his front face in cool ambient shadow 
from the wave wall. High contrast — 
but the shadows carry Ektar's characteristic 
color density rather than pure black.

No grade simulation. No vintage fade. 
Ektar grain throughout — visible in the 
deep lacquer shadow valleys, 
suppressed at gold-halo highlights, 
medium presence on the surfer's suit.

Mood: the instant before the wave erases itself — 
when the material breaks its own coherence 
and releases everything it was holding inside. 
The rider is not conquering this. 
He is inscribing himself into the last moment 
of the wave's structural integrity, 
before it becomes gold dust and cobalt sky.

16:9 vertical, 35mm film photograph, close-up portrait of a person holding a sliced papaya.

Head and hands in the frame, tightly cropped from the bridge of the nose down to the hands. The bottom part of a straw hat is pulled low, just above the eyes, casting a soft shadow on the face. The gaze is directed down at the papaya. Hands are holding the halved papaya open, near the bottom of the frame, with fingertips visible.

Environment:

Outdoors under bright, diffused daylight, likely on a beach or near vegetation. Background is heavily blurred into a warm, sandy-textured bokeh.

Materials & textures:

Natural woven straw hat with visible fibrous texture.

Papaya skin: green and yellow-orange with slight natural blemishes and fine surface dust.

Papaya flesh: vibrant, deep orange with visible graininess.

Papaya seeds: numerous, dark brown, spherical seeds with a moist, slightly coated appearance.

Skin: Natural, sun-kissed skin texture with visible pores and slight natural blemishes, especially around the lips and nose. Hands have subtle sand grains on them.

Nails: Finished with a subtle, textured, silver-grey metallic polish.

Primary focus (food and skin realism):

Deep orange papaya flesh is moist and granular.

Countless, dark, glossy seeds are individual and distinct.

Skin texture is visible, with pores and slight imperfections (no airbrushing).

Tiny, realistic sand grains adhere to fingertips and hands.

Hand-holding the fruit shows natural tension.

Color & light:

Warm, natural light; skin tones are golden and authentic. No harsh flash. Contrast is moderate. Colors are rich and saturated, true-to-life for the ripe fruit. White balance is slightly warm, consistent with natural sunlight.

Camera behavior:

Grainy 35mm film stock. Shallow depth of field: the papaya and the lower face/hands are relatively in focus, with a rapid focus falloff into a soft, textured background. Natural lens characteristic with slight film noise. No over-sharpening.

Overall aesthetic:

Candid, documentary-style, editorial, intimate, natural, authentic. Feels like a real moment captured during travel, not a posed product shot.

STRICT NEGATIVES
beauty filters, skin smoothing, airbrushed look, washed-out colors, desaturated, fake HDR, light bloom, studio lighting, commercial product shot, artificial grain, plasticky textures, text, logos, watermarks

primary_lineage: Lifestyle / candid-performático
secondary_influence: Documental / fotojornalístico
direction_spectrum_score: 4
vocabulary_register:
required_terms: staged-spontaneity, unguarded, light-as-protagonist, effortless, raw authenticity
forbidden_terms: rigid, choreographed, studio-precision, controlled, polished, art-directed
All descriptive language in this prompt is governed by this register — required terms must appear; forbidden terms are categorically excluded.

[SUBJECT :: CORPO E EXPRESSÃO]
Subject is a young woman viewed from a close rear-quarter perspective mounted on a scooter or motorcycle, captured in a state of effortless and staged-spontaneity street realism. The head and face are out of frame above, directing full visual weight to the torso alignment, hip posture, and casual urban attire. She wears an oversized black cotton pullover hoodie featuring a circular stylized graphic illustration on the back with bold graphic typography and comic-style character accents in red, green, and white. Below the hem of the relaxed hoodie, she wears fitted, washed black/charcoal denim micro-shorts with visible double flap-pockets on the rear, exposed contrast topstitching, subtle fraying, and a worn wash texture. The mood is unguarded, relaxed, and anchored in youth street culture.

[BODY MECHANICS :: ANATOMIA INDEPENDENTE]
weight_distribution: Body weight is shifted downward into the scooter seat with natural hip compression, tilted slightly towards the vehicle's leaning axis.
torso_pelvis_counter_rotation: Subtle dynamic counter-rotation between the pelvis seated on the bike saddle and the upper torso reaching forward toward the handlebars.
spine_curve: Gentle natural lumbar lordosis dictated by sitting forward on a low scooter saddle, avoiding mannequin-straight flatness.
shoulder_asymmetry: Asymmetrical shoulder drop; the right shoulder is slightly lifted and protracted forward to grip the handlebar, while the left shoulder sits relaxed.
head_neck_position: Torso extends upward with neck implied angled forward in riding stance.
arm_hand_independence: The right arm reaches forward toward the blurred foreground handlebar grip and brake lever; left arm is positioned forward on the opposite side out of frame, maintaining realistic human asymmetry.
anatomical_verification: Natural tissue compression at the gluteal fold against the seat and thigh contact points; realistic pelvic tilt; organic fold of the shorts conforming to body contours under gravity and movement.
Avoid: perfectly symmetrical posture, rigid mannequin stance, distorted hip-to-thigh proportions, unnatural seamless clothing melting into skin.

[SURFACE :: CABELO, PELE E MAQUIAGEM]
hair: Not visible within the tight crop of the upper back.
skin: Fair-to-light natural skin tone visible on the lower thighs; smooth natural texture with genuine skin pore structure, subtle subsurface scattering under natural ambient sunlight, free of artificial smoothing or heavy plastic sheen.
makeup: Not applicable due to cropped framing focusing on torso and hips.

[OBJECTS / SPACE :: AMBIENTE E INVENTÁRIO]
environment_inventory: Black rubber textured handlebar grip and silver metallic brake lever dominating the out-of-focus lower-left foreground; plastic matte/glossy scooter body panel in deep magenta or dark plum; blurred sunlit outdoor asphalt street; lush green foliage and blurred tree canopy in the upper-left background under open sky.
atmosphere: Raw authenticity and unforced street vitality, capturing a casual roadside moment with light-as-protagonist cutting through the outdoor greenery.
materials: Washed heavy cotton jersey, coarse twill denim with contrast thread, matte rubber handlebar, reflective metal lever, smooth vehicle plastic.

[LIGHT & OPTICS :: ILUMINAÇÃO E ASSINATURA TÉCNICA]
lighting: Natural outdoor daylight, directional soft sunlight arriving from the upper rear-side, producing clean highlights along the fold lines of the hoodie and the rounded surfaces of the denim shorts, with soft open shadows in the recesses.
camera_signature: Fast prime lens aesthetic on a full-frame sensor, very shallow depth of field; extreme foreground handlebar elements exhibit heavy creamy optical bokeh, sharp focal plane directly locked onto the texture and stitching of the rear denim pockets, dropping off softly into blurred background greenery.
lens: 50mm f/1.4 lens equivalent, wide open aperture.
white_balance: Natural daylight balance (~5400K) with cool ambient greens in the shadows and warm neutral highlights on clothing fabrics.

[COLOR GRADE :: MATIZ E CONTRASTE]
temperature: Neutral daylight balance with clean outdoor neutrality and subtle green-cast bounce in shadows.
saturation: Moderate, editorial-balanced street palette; deep charcoal blacks, vibrant pop of red and green inside the back graphic print, natural muted skin tones.
contrast: Balanced contrast with deep organic blacks in the hoodie folds and clean, unclipped highlights on the fabric weave.
shadows: Neutral dark gray with soft open detail, no muddy digital crushing.
highlights: Contained, natural roll-off on fabric highlights and sunlight bouncing off the motorcycle lever.
color_science_connotation: Modern digital cinema capture with gentle film-like highlight roll-off and natural organic tone curves.

[COMPOSITION :: ENQUADRAMENTO E PROFUNDIDADE]
framing: Tight medium close-up focused on the lower torso, hips, and lower back; cut off just below the shoulders and at the upper thighs; low to mid-level Dutch-angled camera tilted slightly along the diagonal of the scooter frame.
point_of_view: Intimate, roadside candid angle positioned just behind and over the right handlebar.
foreground_elements: Heavily blurred scooter handlebar, throttle grip, and brake lever occupying the left foreground to provide dimensional depth framing.
background: Softly rendered, out-of-focus suburban street environment with diffused foliage and daylight bokeh.
depth_of_field: Ultra-shallow plane of focus critically locked on the back pocket seams of the denim shorts and lower graphic print of the sweatshirt.

[ANATOMICAL REINFORCEMENT :: CHECKLIST DE CORREÇÃO]
Ensure: realistic pelvic angle seated against bike saddle; natural soft tissue deformation at thigh contact zones; authentic fabric tension folds extending diagonally from hips and waistband; anatomically sound hip-to-lumbar transitions; correct asymmetry between upper body reach and lower body seating posture.

[NEGATIVE PROMPT :: EXCLUSÕES DINÂMICAS]
rigid, choreographed, studio-precision, controlled, polished, art-directed, studio lighting, posed expression, mannequin posture, perfect symmetry, plastic skin, beauty filter, fake airbrushing, extra limbs, fused clothing, blurry focus on shorts, oversaturated neon grading, artificial HDR glow, visible text errors, watermarks, corporate logos.

[ASPECT RATIO]

POSE & GESTURE: Female subject with sleek, pulled-back hairstyle (tight low bun). The "One Eye Covered" pose: Her left hand is held vertically directly in front of her left eye, palm facing inward. The fingers are elegantly extended, completely obscuring the left eye. The right eye is fully visible, looking intensely at the camera. ::

HANDS & JEWELRY [Macro Detail]: Hand model quality. Long, slender fingers with glossy dark mocha (brown) nail polish. High-fidelity texture on pearls (luster) and metal (reflection). ::

OUTFIT & ATMOSPHERE: Wearing a matte black turtleneck sweater that blends seamlessly into the deep, dark brown/black background (Low Key aesthetic). Floating head and hand effect. ::

LIGHTING & OPTICS: Soft directional studio lighting hitting the visible side of the face and the back of the hand. Deep shadows on the obscured side (Chiaroscuro). Shot on 100mm Macro lens, f/5.6 (to keep both eye and rings in focus), sharp texture on skin pores and iris --ar 3:4

He is wearing a tattered, sweat-soaked red athletic jersey (tank top style) that reveals his immense, muscular chest and shoulders.

ART STYLE: 1990s comic book cover aesthetic with heavy stippling and cross-hatching textures. The style should feel gritty and visceral, similar to classic sports posters. Use vibrant, saturated colors with a "rough" grain finish.

Emphasize micro-details like the saliva in the mouth, individual fur strands, and the damaged leather of the ball. Cinematic composition, low angle to emphasize power and scale. 8k resolution, masterpiece quality.

[IDENTITY LOCK]
一位年轻的东亚女性，拥有中等偏小的骨架，明显的丰满梨形/沙漏型身材：窄肩、上半身丰满但胸廓不宽、腰部纤细收束、骨盆和髋部非常宽阔、臀部体积丰满、厚实、圆润并向后突出，大腿根部粗壮饱满。整体轮廓是窄肩＋细腰＋极宽胯＋非常丰满臀部＋厚实大腿。

Primary_lineage: Ultra-realistic photograph. Secondary_influence: High-end editorial fashion lookbook. Direction_spectrum_score: 9 (highly composed, editorial impact). Vocabulary_register: Required terms: skin texture, fabric tension, natural light, lens perspective. Forbidden terms: smooth skin, perfect symmetry, flat lighting, heavy bokeh, muscular butt, jeans, skirt, black hair, straight hair, short bob, flash, night shot.

[SUBJECT :: CORPO E EXPRESSÃO]
Description: 该年轻东亚女性以背面三分之四侧身姿态站在镜前自拍。Expression: 表情安静、冷淡，眼睛看向镜中的手机屏幕。不露齿笑。Clothing: 上身穿一件纯黑色紧身长袖短款上衣，柔软高弹棉质罗纹面料，紧贴上半身和纤细腰线，圆领，露出明显一段腰腹和后腰。下身穿一条非常短的豹纹贴身热裤，底色为浅米色，上面布满大小不一的深棕色和黑色不规则玫瑰状豹纹斑点，裤腰位于低腰位置，紧贴宽阔髋部，裤腿极短，包覆臀部和大腿根部。脚上穿着一双简约的米白色软皮居家拖鞋。Accessories: 右手竖直握一部浅色三摄智能手机，手机壳为奶白底，带浅粉、米色蝴蝶 Y2K 小图案。手指可见少量小型手指纹身、金色戒指和浅粉裸色美甲。Pose: 身体大部分背对镜子，但上半身向人物左侧回转约30-40°，头部转向镜面形成三分之四侧脸。骨盆明显向人物右后方推出，腰部向相反方向收紧，形成强烈 S 型曲线。双腿自然站立，靠近镜头的一侧腿略微向前、膝盖放松，另一侧腿承担主要重心。右手向前伸向镜面自拍，左手自然垂在身体后侧，手掌轻轻靠近臀部下缘。

[BODY MECHANICS :: ANATOMIA INDEPENDENTE]
Weight_distribution: 重心明显落在远离镜头的左腿上，右腿膝盖放松微屈。Torso_pelvis_counter_rotation: 骨盆严重向右后方（画面右侧）推出，上半身则向左转动（朝向镜面），腰部形成深度不对称收束。Spine_curve: 腰椎形成深刻的侧向 S 形曲线，展现极大的腰臀差。Shoulder_asymmetry: 抬起手机的右肩明显高于放松的左肩。Head_neck_position: 头部紧接着上半身继续转向镜面，颈部拉长，形成自然的三分之四侧脸。Arm_hand_independence: 右臂从肩膀自然伸向镜面，产生真实近大远小透视，手机位于画面左前方；左臂放松垂在后侧，手掌轻轻贴在臀腿连接处，手指自然弯曲。Anatomical_integrity: 臀部和髋部必须表现为柔软的脂肪组织和自然重力，严禁健美肌肉轮廓、异常球形、穿模或没有布料厚度的质感。Avoid: Frontal pose, symmetrical shoulders, straight spine, flat hips, symmetrical hips, tensed arm, hands in pockets.

[SURFACE :: CABELO, PELE E MAQUIAGEM]
Hair: 深冷棕色带自然灰褐色调的中长发，发丝呈现自然的波浪纹理，发量丰盈蓬松，长度及肩下，发尾自然散落。额前为轻薄空气刘海，长度接近眉毛，中央略稀疏。Skin: 白皙偏暖的肤色，保留真实皮肤毛孔和细微肤色变化。Makeup: 小巧扁鹅蛋形脸，深棕色杏仁眼，双眼皮自然，眼线纤细略微上扬，睫毛清晰；眉毛自然偏平。鼻梁小巧，鼻尖精致，嘴唇自然丰满，裸粉豆沙色。

[OBJECTS / SPACE :: AMBIENTE E INVENTÁRIO]
Setting: 明亮的现代极简卧室/公寓。Background: 人物身后中央偏右是一台大型黑色壁挂电视（关闭状态），屏幕有轻微反光；电视右侧是一扇明亮窗户，可以看到模糊的绿色树木和室外自然光。画面右下方可见一张简约白色床架，床上铺深海军蓝/黑蓝色被子。左侧背景是一扇白色室内门、浅色门框、白色电灯开关和插座。Floor: 浅木色木纹地板。Atmosphere: 干净、明亮、真实居家感。

[LIGHT & OPTICS :: ILUMINAÇÃO E ASSINATURA TÉCNICA]
Lighting: 以白天自然窗光（来自右侧 Janela）为主，辅以柔和室内环境光。右侧窗户提供稍强侧光，在头发、肩部、腰侧和臀胯边缘形成轻微明亮轮廓。Skin, cloth textures clearly defined. Camera_signature: 真实手机镜面自拍透视，轻微手机 HDR、自然数码锐化。Lens: 28mm f/2.8 equivalent phone lens. White_balance: Auto natural daylight, slightly warm.

[COLOR GRADE :: MATIZ E CONTRASTE]
Temperature: Natural daylight, slight warmth from window. Saturation: Natural, desaturated whites, deep blacks, muted warm tones. Contrast: Moderate, keeping details in shadows (black top, shadows) and highlights (white wall, skin).

[COMPOSITION :: ENQUADRAMENTO E PROFUNDIDADE]
Framing: Cuerpo entero (full body), including the feet and floor. Point_of_view: Eye-level mirror reflection, capturing the entire subject and room context. Foreground_elements: The right hand and phone in the immediate mirror perspective, scaled naturally. Background: Modern minimalist bedroom, with large black TV and window visible behind the subject. Depth_of_field: Background elements like the bed and TV are clear, no portrait mode bokeh.

[ANATOMICAL REINFORCEMENT :: CHECKLIST DE CORREÇÃO]
Pear-shaped silhouette: YES. Narrow shoulders, slim waist, very wide hips, voluminous soft butt, thick upper thighs. Body mechanics: YES. Weight shift to left leg, pelvis pushed right, upper body rotated left, asymmetrical shoulders and hips, natural S-curve spine. Independence: YES. Head turn separate from torso, arm extension naturally scaled. Textures: YES. Real skin pores, hair definition, rib knit tension, leopard pattern stretching, no clipping. Avoidance check: YES. No straight spine, no flatness, no muscular butt definition.

[NEGATIVE PROMPT :: EXCLUSÕES DINÂMICAS]
正面站姿、人物完全背对镜头看不到脸、对称肩部、平板腰、窄胯、扁臀、细大腿、健美肌肉臀、异常球形臀、腰臀差不足、黑色长裤、牛仔短裤、裙子、豹纹变虎纹、裤腿过长、手机过小、手臂消失、手臂粗大畸形、裸露上半身、性感挑逗表情、复杂豪华卧室、夜景、强闪光、棚拍硬光、人像模式奶油虚化、鱼眼镜头、长发、卷发、厚齐刘海、黑发、短 Bob、直发、身體builder、肌肉線條分明、血管明顯、六塊腹肌、競賽體型、過於瘦弱、平板身材、沒有曲線、水印、文字。

items.title: ee2be95b-2071-4fd0-a85a-1174a67d8ec2
items.rawPrompt:
Vintage offset-print collage aesthetic — analog source photography
composited with flat graphic design elements drawn from 1960s–70s
travel poster design and Japanese silkscreen printing.
Source photography reference: Kodachrome 64, warm shadow
saturation, shot on medium format Rolleiflex 2.8F 80mm Planar,
natural morning light. No digital rendering feel —
this is printed matter, not a screen.

The scene: the intricate mangrove forests of Soure, Ilha de Marajó,
at high tide — ancient aerial roots, the dense, humid canopy,
a labyrinth of brackish water channels. The sky occupies the upper
half of the frame and has been entirely replaced by a halftone dot field:
cobalt blue dots on cornflower ground, the mechanical rhythm
of offset printing standing in for the atmosphere.
No photographic surface texture — only the grid of the press.

Below the skyline, the mangrove architecture rises
as documentary photography: real, unretouched, carrying
emulsion grain and Kodachrome warmth. But every massive root curve,
every arching prop root, every silhouette of a distant ibis has been
color-filled with flat coral red — as if the graphic system
has classified all organic architecture under a single category:
the monumental. A perfect circle, flat and vectorial,
coral red, no gradient, no outline, sits between
two mangrove trunks in the lower register.
It does not glow. It declares itself as fact.

A single photographic figure — a vaqueiro de búfalo (buffalo cowboy),
contemporary, real, riding a submerged beast through the channel —
moves through the middle ground,
unmodified against the graphic foliage behind him.
He does not look at the camera.
He moves as if the graphic transformation
of his island is simply the weather.

In the mud register, halftone dots swell toward the corners —
a vignette built from the logic of printing, not optics.
Three distant guarantee birds are pure black silhouette:
no photography, no detail — flat cutouts
placed like typographic marks on the water line.

At all four edges: a dashed red-and-white border frame —
the language of the souvenir, the travel brochure,
the thing that was designed to be kept.

items.title: cfecb723-ab18-499f-a69a-5138b8cb779e
items.rawPrompt:
Shot from just above the material surface, large format analog 
aesthetic, Pentax 67 with SMC 300mm f/4 ED telephoto, 
Kodak Ektar 100 pushed one stop for maximum chroma saturation 
and compressed tonal range.

A surfer — male, lean, crouched low into a hard committed 
carving turn — rides the inner face of a massive wave that 
is not water. The wave has been transmuted: its entire body 
is flowing Japanese urushi lacquer, deep crimson-black, 
with rivers of raw gold running through its mass like veins 
of kintsugi repair work embedded inside the structure 
before it ever broke. The lacquer reads as liquid in motion — 
it swells, curls and pitches with the geometry of ocean 
hydrology, but its surface is non-aqueous: no foam, no 
refraction — only gloss, depth, and material weight.

The surfer's suit is a single-piece deep crimson latex, 
wet-sheen, color-matched to the wave's dominant tone — 
as if he was cast from the same material he rides. 
His right arm trails, fingertips grazing the lacquer wall. 
The contact point leaves no splash — only a drawn line, 
a calligraphic mark in the surface of the wave, 
as if he is writing something.

The foreground holds suspended gold-leaf fragments — 
irregular, non-circular, drifting slowly in a plane 
between the lens and the subject. Not bokeh: these 
are physical flakes, each catching and fracturing the 
ambient light differently, creating a semi-translucent 
interference layer through which the rider is perceived. 
No water droplets. No foam particles. Only the residue 
of the wave's own material logic dispersed into air.

The sky above the wave crest: absolute cobalt, 
ungraded, no sun — zero horizon, zero atmosphere. 
The light source cannot be identified. The lacquer 
emits its own luminosity through internal reflection, 
warming the underside of the curl from within. 
The rider is lit by what the wave carries, not what 
falls from above.

Camera angle: low Dutch, 15° tilt clockwise, 
the wave diagonal cutting top-left to bottom-right 
across the frame. Telephoto compression collapses 
all depth — the distant wave crest and the near 
gold-leaf veil appear to occupy the same plane, 
the surfer suspended between layers of the same material 
at different states of coherence.

COLOR PALETTE 60/30/10:
60% — deep crimson-lacquer black (#4A0F0F / #6B1A1A) 
as the wave mass — opaque, light-absorbing in its valleys, 
mirror-glossy at its crests.
30% — raw gold-amber vein (#C8922A / #A67820) 
threading through the lacquer structure and dispersed 
as fragment-bokeh in the foreground plane.
10% — absolute cobalt sky (#0D2B6B) 
as the single neutral field against which 
the wave's entire material excess is measured.

LIGHTING:
No directional source. No golden hour. No sun disc. 
All luminosity is emissive — reflected internally 
through the lacquer's own glossy surface logic. 
The rider is warm-lit by proximity to the material, 
not by external fill. Shadows are absolute where 
the lacquer folds on itself: no lifted blacks, 
no vintage fade — this is not nostalgia. 
It is density.

Ektar grain structure throughout — 
coarser in the deep shadow valleys of the wave, 
almost absent at the gold-vein highlights.

Mood: surfing as a ritual act performed inside 
a material that should not move but does — 
the rider not conquering the wave 
but tracing its inner logic from within.

items.rawPrompt:
[SYSTEM ROLE]
You are an expert visual analyst specializing in Personal Color Theory (12-season expanded system), Facial Geometry (Visagism by Philip Hallawell), and Body Typology (Kibbe System). Your task is to perform a structured visual analysis and render a high-fidelity editorial infographic.

---

[PHASE 1 — SILENT VISUAL EXTRACTION]
Before generating any visual output, internally extract and resolve the following parameters from the provided reference image. Do NOT skip this phase.

A. SKIN UNDERTONE ANALYSIS
   — Map the visible skin to a precise undertone: Warm (golden/peachy/yellow base), Cool (pink/blue/rosy base), or Neutral.
   — Identify the exact dominant hex code of the skin's mid-tone (not the lightest highlight or darkest shadow).
   — Classify the seasonal archetype: Spring / Summer / Autumn / Winter (and sub-type if visible: e.g. "True Autumn", "Soft Summer").

B. CONTRAST MAPPING
   — Measure the visual contrast between: (1) skin vs. hair, (2) skin vs. eyes.
   — Classify as: Low, Medium, or High contrast.
   — This contrast level determines the chromatic weight (saturation + value) that garments must carry.

### PROMPT: TRANS-DIMENSIONAL MATCHA EFFERVESCENCE

**STYLE & MOOD:** Hyper-realistic macro photography, editorial food & beverage aesthetic. High-contrast, vibrant, and tactile. The mood is refreshing yet surreal, focusing on the physics of carbonation and frozen textures.

**SUBJECT:** An extreme close-up top-down view of a thick, vibrant lime-green matcha foam or wheatgrass smoothie. Submerged within the foam are several large, jagged, rectangular ice blocks that appear dark, almost like obsidian or frozen deep-green sap.

**TEXTURE & DETAILS:** The green liquid is densely packed with thousands of tiny, uniform micro-bubbles and larger effervescent spheres, creating a frothy, porous texture reminiscent of sea foam or cellular structures. The ice blocks show internal fractures, frosted surfaces, and trapped air bubbles, creating a sharp contrast against the soft, aerated liquid.

**LIGHTING & COLOR:** Directional hard lighting from the top-right, creating deep, dramatic shadows and bright, specular highlights on the bubbles' surfaces. The palette is dominated by electric neon green, deep forest shadows, and translucent gray-scale tones in the ice.

**PHOTOGRAPHY SPECS:** Shot on a Hasselblad H6D-100c with a 120mm f/4 Macro lens. Extreme depth of field focused on the surface bubbles. 8k resolution, ultra-sharp details showing every individual bubble membrane and the crystalline texture of the ice. No airbrushing; maintain natural liquid imperfections.
